text:
Marta: Heads-up: onboarding reports keep saying "something went wrong" in python SDKs. TS users get a typed exception. We should standardize before next release.
Sahil: saw a support ticket where a customer blamed their code for a 502 because message was just 'request failed'. we need clearer remediation hints. :confused: 
Kevin: agreed. cross-sdk parity is the bigger pain. different class names and different properties. hard for multi-lang teams.
Olivia: would like a tiny "Failures" section in quickstart showing how to catch and handle errors in each SDK. simple examples only.
Marta: proposal: 1) stable Error class names (AuthError, PermissionError, NotFoundError, RateLimitError, TimeoutError, ServerError, StreamError), 2) each error carries code (string), retryable (true|false), request_id, hint_url.
Sahil: mapping sketch I used in support: 
```
401 -> AuthError(code="invalid_api_key", retryable=false)
403 -> PermissionError(code="policy_denied", retryable=false)
404 -> NotFoundError(code="model_not_found", retryable=false)
408,504 -> TimeoutError(code="upstream_timeout", retryable=true)
429 -> RateLimitError(code="rate_limit", retryable=true, retry_after=secs)
5xx -> ServerError(code="server_error", retryable=true)
stream-chunk-error -> StreamError(code="chunk_failure", recoverable=true, offset=12345)
```
Kevin: important: include the machine code string in the human message too so teams can programmatically branch and also read it in logs. e.g., "Rate limit exceeded (code=rate_limit). Retry after 12s. See: /docs/throughput"
Olivia: UX constraints: short sentence + one next step + link. no raw stack traces in messages. logs/telemetry can carry full traces.
Sahil: implement approach: throw native Error subclass (language idiomatic) with attached fields: error.code, error.retryable, error.hint_url, error.request_id. Python: subclass Exception; TS: extend Error. keep try/catch normal.
Kevin: and for languages that prefer envelope responses (some RPCs) provide a helper: to_error(envelope) -> raise or return depending on caller preference.
Marta: ops-bot, create a tracking task for SDK parity + docs with owners and due date.
ops-bot: Created task RDW-UX-1289: "SDK error surface alignment: classes, codes, docs" assigned to @sahil, @olivia, due 2026-04-10.
Olivia: doc copy suggestions for quickstart:
- AuthError: "Authentication failed. Check API key or token expiry. See /docs/auth. (code=invalid_api_key)"
- RateLimitError: "Rate limit exceeded. Pause and retry in Xs or lower concurrency. See /docs/throughput. (code=rate_limit)"
- NotFoundError: "Model not found. List available models with /models. (code=model_not_found)"
Sahil: add request_id to every error message: "Request id: abc123". makes server-side lookups trivial. also emit structured telemetry: error.code, http_status, request_id, sdk_name, sdk_version.
Kevin: CI lint idea: require tests that assert errors expose code + retryable + request_id. small enforcement but helps parity.
Marta: streaming nuance: if a chunk fails mid-stream we should decide between: 1) emit StreamError with position and let app resume, or 2) abort whole stream. recommend StreamError with recoverable flag and position.
Olivia: onboarding tweak: add a one-liner in SDK install flow about how to get help: "When in doubt include request_id and code when filing a ticket."
Sahil: implementation plan: 
- day 0: spec doc + enums for codes
- day 1-3: patch runtime mapping in python and ts SDKs
- day 4: tests + CI lint rule
- day 5: docs + quickstart updates
Estimate per SDK ~3 working days, but we can parallelize.
Kevin: when you post the PR please include examples for both sync and async/streaming paths.
Marta: thanks. small change but big reduction in support time. :thumbsup:
Sahil: I'll post a WIP PR link here once ready.
Olivia: can review copy and make it customer-friendly.
Marta: great. follow-up: we'll measure support triage time and number of ambiguous tickets.
